competitive_landscape: İzmir Bay is run today by the municipal İZDENİZ sea-bus operator on conventional diesel vessels — and crucially, the city already commutes by water at scale (~14.6M trips/yr), so demand is proven rather than speculative. The Çeşme↔Chios crossing is served by conventional fast-craft (Ertürk Lines). The status quo we improve on is slow, diesel and unmodernised; the opportunity is a clean, faster, smoother foiling tier on an artery the public has already adopted.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Every route here is comfortably all-electric: the İzmir Bay commuter mesh (~3–6 nm), İzmir↔Çeşme (~45 nm) and Çeşme↔Chios (~7 nm) all sit well inside the 70 nm envelope — ideal for high-frequency, high-rotation public-transit and leisure service available now.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not needed for the bay or the Chios hop; Quanta-LR would only come into play to extend the network onward along the wider Aegean (e.g. toward the Çeşme–Bodrum coast) as it grows.

precedents.what: $100M, ~100-vessel electric-hydrofoil network with JIH Global, phased over 3 years (first 5 vessels in 2026)
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows an all-electric foiling network financed and deployed at national scale — confidence that a clean upgrade to a proven, high-volume water-transit market is bankable.

precedents.what: An established municipal sea-bus network carrying ~14.6M passengers a year since 1992
precedents.why_it_matters: Local proof that water-commuting works and is embraced at scale here — Navier modernises a habit that already exists rather than creating a new one.

regulatory_note: İzmir is run by a CHP municipality whose İZDENİZ unit is the public-transport authority for the bay — a municipal clean-fleet channel parallel to (and distinct from) Istanbul's İBB. Turkey is Navier's factory market, giving home classification via Türk Loydu. The Çeşme↔Chios crossing runs through established Turkish/Greek CIQ ferry ports.
seasonality: İzmir Bay is sheltered and serviceable year-round, with the heaviest leisure demand May–Sept. The summer meltemi (etesian) NW wind raises afternoon chop in the open Aegean toward Çeşme — conditions where foiling's smoother, faster ride is the premium over a conventional ferry. Winter service stays robust on the protected bay.
signature_routes: Karşıyaka ↔ Konak (İzmir Bay sea-bus upgrade, all-electric)
summary: İzmir is the rare Turkish city where commuting by water is already a daily habit: the municipal İZDENİZ sea-bus network carries ~14.6 million passengers a year across the bay (Karşıyaka↔Konak and beyond). Just west, Çeşme and Alaçatı form an upscale Aegean beach scene, and Çeşme sits only ~7 nm from the Greek island of Chios. This is a city with both a heavy, validated urban-ferry artery ripe for a clean, fast upgrade and a high-end leisure corridor — the textbook pairing of public-transit and tourism demand on one bay.
tagline: İzmir already moves 14 million people a year across its bay by sea — on slow diesel ferries. The demand is proven; the experience is decades old.
